required: postgres: transaction rollback, concurrent completions and stale progress writes
postgres: playlist reads/writes reject anonymous sessions
Redis atomically shares request limits across independent application instances
postgres: account writes serialize concurrent field changes and roll back atomically
postgres: cross-device CAS permits one simultaneous writer and rejects stale device state
postgres: populated revision migration preserves progress, completion, events and old client high-water marks
postgres: rejected valid attempts also reserve their identity and cannot be repurposed
postgres: progress survives Redis disconnect/reconnect and streaming remains available
postgres: concurrent history removal and progress updates serialize without resurrection
postgres: guarded bulk clear is atomic, repeat-safe and does not erase post-clear activity
postgres: additive history migration preserves bookmarks, completion and revision receipts

databaseChanges.writes: Transactions with owner-before-chapter lock ordering; owner lock serializes bulk clear/progress/read guard; SQLite uses existing serialized adapter
databaseChanges.preservation: Fresh and populated migrations/reapply, SQLite import of tombstones and retained target tombstones, actual 21-table PostgreSQL backup/restore fingerprints all pass

apiChanges: GET /api/history?limit=20&cursor=... default20/max50, exact timestamp/chapter DESC owner-bound cursor; returns entries,nextCursor,historyRevision
DELETE /api/history/:chapterId with expectedRevision; generic success for missing/foreign entries
DELETE /api/history with expectedHistoryRevision and confirm:CLEAR_SAVED_HISTORY; repeat-empty no-op, new activity conflicts
GET current chapter/story chapters expose removed; Continue Listening and visible progress list exclude tombstones

changes: Hide saved bookmarks from History and Continue Listening
Clear incomplete saved positions to zero
Preserve row/revision tombstone; increment chapter revision once
Advance owner history revision once per removal/bulk operation
Retain old receipt/high-water identities; stale writes conflict; ordinary saves cannot restore tombstones
Explicit current-revision reset/replay can restore saved progress
retains: Completion flags and completed end markers
Listening events/time totals, analytics rollups and outbox
deletionSemantics.idempotency: Repeated individual removal acknowledges existing tombstone without another increment. Empty bulk clear is a no-op; old clear after new activity returns409. Old accepted write retries acknowledge original outcome but return current tombstone, never restore old data.
deletionSemantics.privacy: Bookmark removal is not full data erasure; future playback can still generate listening analytics. No analytics/account deletion API added.

testsCover: Cursor limits/defaults/ties/deleted boundaries/PG microseconds/foreign and malformed cursors
Individual and guarded bulk removal/duplicate removal
Stale device writes, exact prior receipts and explicit replay
Concurrent delete-update and bulk-clear-update races, proven transaction rollback
Redis disconnect503 for private history, public range206, recovery and no catalog cache use
Guest upgrade, login/logout, refresh, pending history reads/mutations during account changes
Active audio/queue continuity, old queued resets and autoplay cannot restore known tombstones
Offline cache exclusion, downloads/range/storage-error and existing player/analytics/progress regressions

limitations: Removal retains tombstones/receipts/completion/analytics/backups and does not provide full privacy erasure
Live cursor pages require refresh to see newer/moved entries; active playback can cause an intentional stale-clear409
Old /progress list remains unpaginated for backward compatibility
Owner-level locking prioritizes correctness; no new load/performance claims
Replace/drain old API binaries before enabling removals; old binaries do not enforce tombstones
Restoring older backups can restore older state/revisions; retire offline writers during recovery
Queues remain tab-local; downloads device-wide/public; history management requires an online authenticated session
No general durable offline write queue, creator features or cross-device queue synchronization
